title: Finite local dimension for finite type schemes over a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $x\in X$. Then the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has finite Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Lemma "lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field" (Tag 00P1), together with the affine finite-type localization argument

proof.text: Every ideal of the field $K$ is either $(0)$ or $(1)$: an ideal containing a nonzero $a$ contains $a^{-1}a=1$. Thus every ideal is finitely generated and $K$ is Noetherian. The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has global section ring $K$ and one point. Its single affine chart is a Noetherian affine cover, and a one-point space is quasi-compact. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is Noetherian.

Apply the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem to the given structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its target is Noetherian by step 1, so $X$ is Noetherian and in particular locally Noetherian.

Choose a member $U$ of the Noetherian affine covering of $X$ containing $x$, and set $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$; its ring is Noetherian by the definition of locally Noetherian. The affine-open stalk-localization theorem, clause (c), says that the germ map $R	o\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a localization at the complement of the corresponding prime $\mathfrak p_x$. This complement is multiplicative: $1
otin\mathfrak p_x$, and $s,t
otin\mathfrak p_x$ implies $st
otin\mathfrak p_x$ by primality. Apply the localization-Noetherian theorem directly to this germ map to conclude that $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian. It is a local ring because $X$ is a locally ringed space.

proof.text: Apply the finiteness clause of the Noetherian-local-system-of-parameters theorem to $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, which is Noetherian and local by step 3. It gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}<\infty$, exactly the desired conclusion; none of its additional system-of-parameters conclusions is needed.
